Hi Sofia —

Hope you and the team are doing well. As we approach your Oct 2027 renewal, I wanted to start the conversation around the usage profile you've been seeing and a few structured options to cover the anticipated product launch traffic spike you mentioned on the last call.

Attached: a fresh draft with two renewal options (pdf) and your usage export from Q3/Q4 (csv). TL;DR of what we'd like to align on:
- A 12-month price-hold window to protect against model-price volatility while you scale.
- A temporary burst pool for up to 30% above committed throughput for the first 90 days post-launch.
- A credit overlay we can apply to uneven usage months so you don't materially overpay while you tune caching/batching.

Can we align on a working session next week? The three options in the pdf are: Option A (multi-year aggressive commit + deeper discount), Option B (12-month price hold + moderate commit + burst pool), Option C (no commit, increased unit price, flexible true-up). I think Option B hits the balance for ConvergentAI given the launch runway you described.

Available windows: Thu 11/19 10–11am PT or Fri 11/20 9–10am PT. Happy to loop in Marissa and Ben for finance/structure questions.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Rafael —

Thanks for starting this. A couple quick items from our side after reviewing the PDF:

1) The launch is currently slated for mid-Jan 2027 and we expect a 3–4x spike in inference volume for ~6 weeks, then a sustained +40% baseline. We need a solution that avoids emergency overage invoices while we iterate.
2) Procurement's priority: a 12-month price hold, and some level of consumption credits for the launch window. They will not sign a long-term commit without clearer top-line revenue impact.
3) We also need a simple true-up mechanism for Q1 2027 to reconcile actual vs committed usage.

If you can give us a concrete pricing delta between Option B (your recommended) and Option C (flex/no commit), plus the size of the credit bucket you'd propose for the surge, we can escalate to procurement.

I'm available Thu 11/19 1–2pm PT if you want to talk live.

—Sofia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: capacity uplift + short-term surge strategy

Hi Sofia — Rafael looped me in to share concrete numbers and a recommended structure that aligns with procurement's asks while preserving predictable unit economics. Below are two practical paths we can take. I included simple cost deltas (all numbers illustrative — final in SOW):

Option 1 — Price-hold + modest commit (Recommended)
- Term: 12 months price hold from Jan 1, 2027
- Commitment: 40% of projected annualized baseline (based on your Q4 run-rate)
- Burst pool: Additional 30% capacity available for 90 days after launch at a blended unit price (slightly above committed rate)
- Credit overlay: 200k token-credit bucket to apply against surge months (applied before invoicing)
- Estimated ARR delta vs Option C: -8% unit price improvement
- True-up: single Q1 2027 true-up window to reconcile +/- 15% variance (capacity to purchase additional committed units if above threshold)

Option 2 — Flexible with larger credit (Procurement-favorable)
- Term: 12 months price hold
- Commitment: none (flex)
- Burst pool: 30% available; higher per-token rate than Option 1
- Credit overlay: 350k token-credit bucket to smooth launch costs
- Estimated ARR delta vs Option C: +6% higher unit price but predictable capped surge cost

Key trade-offs: Option 1 reduces unit cost long-term and preserves a controlled true-up cadence; Option 2 gives procurement low contractual commitment but increases the per-unit cost and uses a larger credit fund for the launch.

Next steps: If procurement prefers Option 1, Ben (cc'd) will validate the exact dollar/credit sizing and I can push an Amended SOW + DocuSign to the procurement contact. If Option 2 is preferred, we'll prepare a short-term amendment and a one-page addendum that defines the credit application and burst-rate ceilings.

Attached: a one-page summary of the two options and a sample true-up table. Let me know which direction and we'll get legal/procurement-ready docs moving.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Growth Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (628) 555-0188

- Accept Option 1 structure but reduce committed baseline to 30% (instead of 40%).
- Accept the 30% burst pool for 90 days.
- Increase the credit bucket to 300k tokens, applied across Jan–Mar 2027 as needed.
- Include an explicit Q1 2027 true-up with the option to add committed capacity starting Apr 1 if utilization exceeds 25% above commit for two consecutive months.

If you can update the SOW with the 30% commit and $ credit bucket (we don't publish token $ here; procurement will validate), we can route to DocuSign this week.
